1	# State of the Web 2020–2025: HTTP Archive Trends
     2	
     3	## Source
     4	
     5	HTTP Archive — State of the Web Report  
     6	https://httparchive.org/reports/state-of-the-web?start=2020_01_01&end=latest&view=list
     7	
     8	## Overview
     9	
    10	The HTTP Archive continuously crawls millions of URLs and records how the web is built. The "State of the Web" report tracks macro-level metrics including page weight, request counts, protocol adoption (HTTPS, HTTP/2, HTTP/3), TCP connection counts, and CSS best-practice adoption such as `font-display`. The data below covers January 2020 through early 2026, with desktop and mobile measured separately.
    11	
    12	## Sample Size
    13	
    14	The crawl sample has grown substantially. In January 2020 the desktop crawl covered roughly 5 million URLs and mobile roughly 3.5 million. By mid-2022 both lines jumped sharply — desktop reaching ~15 million and mobile ~10 million — before stabilizing around 16 million (desktop) and 12.5 million (mobile) by mid-2023 onward.
    15	
    16	![Timeseries of Sample Size — Desktop vs Mobile](./assets/figure_1.jpg)
    17	
    18	## Page Weight & Requests
    19	
    20	Median total transfer size has risen gradually over five years. Desktop pages now weigh approximately 2,000 KB (median), up from ~1,600 KB in early 2020. Mobile pages track slightly lower but follow the same upward trend. The 75th-percentile desktop page exceeds 4,000 KB, indicating a long tail of heavy pages.
    21	
    22	![Timeseries of Total Kilobytes — Desktop vs Mobile with IQR bands](./assets/figure_2.jpg)
    23	
    24	The median number of resources requested per page is 76 on desktop and 71 on mobile, each up roughly 3% over the observation period.
    25	
    26	| Metric | Desktop | Mobile | Desktop Δ | Mobile Δ |
    27	|---|---|---|---|---|
    28	| Total Kilobytes (median) | ~2,000 KB | ~1,900 KB | ▲ ~25% | ▲ ~25% |
    29	| Total Requests (median) | 76 | 71 | ▲ 2.7% | ▲ 2.9% |
    30	| TCP Connections / Page (median) | 12.0 | 11.0 | ▼ 14.3% | ▼ 26.7% |
    31	
    32	## TCP Connections Per Page
    33	
    34	Despite growing request counts, the median number of TCP connections per page has fallen — from about 15 (desktop) and 15 (mobile) in early 2020 to 12 and 11 respectively. This decline reflects the multiplexing benefits of HTTP/2 and HTTP/3, which allow many requests over fewer connections.
    35	
    36	![Timeseries of TCP Connections Per Page](./assets/figure_3.jpg)
    37	
    38	## Protocol & Security Adoption
    39	
    40	### HTTPS
    41	
    42	HTTPS adoption is now effectively universal. 99.2% of desktop requests and 99.1% of mobile requests use HTTPS, representing an increase of roughly 19–20 percentage points since early 2020 when adoption was around 80%.
    43	
    44	### HTTP/2
    45	
    46	HTTP/2 accounts for 58.6% of desktop requests and 57.6% of mobile requests. Growth has been modest recently (1–3%), partly because HTTP/3 is absorbing some of the newer adoption.
    47	
    48	### HTTP/3 Support
    49	
    50	HTTP/3 support has seen explosive growth. Desktop support stands at 38.7% and mobile at 40.0%. The percentage increases from the 2020 baseline are enormous (reported as 38,600% desktop and 5,614% mobile) because the starting point was near zero. Note: HTTP Archive measures HTTP/3 *support* rather than actual usage because fresh Chrome instances default to HTTP/2 on first connection before discovering HTTP/3 capability via Alt-Svc headers.
    51	
    52	| Protocol Metric | Desktop | Mobile |
    53	|---|---|---|
    54	| HTTPS Requests | 99.2% | 99.1% |
    55	| HTTP/2 Requests | 58.6% | 57.6% |
    56	| HTTP/3 Support | 38.7% | 40.0% |
    57	
    58	## Font-Display Adoption
    59	
    60	The `font-display` CSS property helps avoid the Flash of Invisible Text (FOIT) during web font loading. As measured by Lighthouse, 40.1% of desktop pages and 42.5% of mobile pages now use this property — up 14.9% and 61.0% respectively since 2020. While adoption is growing, more than half of pages still risk FOIT.
    61	
    62	## Key Findings
    63	
    64	- **Page weight keeps climbing**: Median desktop pages now transfer ~2,000 KB, roughly 25% heavier than in 2020, driven by richer media and JavaScript.
    65	- **HTTPS is the new baseline**: At 99%+ of requests, unencrypted HTTP is essentially extinct on the modern web.
    66	- **HTTP/3 is the fastest-growing protocol metric**: From near-zero to ~40% support in under four years, HTTP/3 is rapidly becoming mainstream.
    67	- **Fewer TCP connections despite more requests**: Multiplexing in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 has cut median connections per page by 15–27%, improving network efficiency.
    68	- **Font-display still underused**: At ~40–42% adoption, there is significant room for improvement in avoiding invisible text during font loading.

    51	
    52	# PPTX Manipulation Skill
    53	
    54	## Overview
    55	
    56	This skill enables programmatic creation, editing, and manipulation of Microsoft PowerPoint (.pptx) presentations using the **python-pptx** library. Create professional slides with text, shapes, images, charts, and tables without manual editing.
    57	
    58	## How to Use
    59	
    60	1. Describe the presentation you want to create or modify
    61	2. Provide content, data, or images to include
    62	3. I'll generate python-pptx code and execute it
    63	
    64	**Example prompts:**
    65	- "Create a 10-slide pitch deck from this outline"
    66	- "Add a chart to slide 3 with this data"
    67	- "Extract all text from this presentation"
    68	- "Generate slides from this markdown content"
    69	
    70	## Domain Knowledge
    71	
    72	### python-pptx Fundamentals
    73	
    74	```python
    75	from pptx import Presentation
    76	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
    77	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
    78	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
    79	
    80	# Create new presentation
    81	prs = Presentation()
    82	
    83	# Or open existing
    84	prs = Presentation('existing.pptx')
    85	```
    86	
    87	### Presentation Structure
    88	```
    89	Presentation
    90	├── slide_layouts (predefined layouts)
    91	├── slides (individual slides)
    92	│   ├── shapes (text, images, charts)
    93	│   │   ├── text_frame (paragraphs)
    94	│   │   └── table (rows, cells)
    95	│   └── placeholders (title, content)
    96	└── slide_masters (templates)
    97	```
    98	
    99	### Slide Layouts
   100	```python
   101	# Common layout indices (may vary by template)
   102	TITLE_SLIDE = 0
   103	TITLE_CONTENT = 1
   104	SECTION_HEADER = 2
   105	TWO_CONTENT = 3
   106	COMPARISON = 4
   107	TITLE_ONLY = 5
   108	BLANK = 6
   109	
   110	# Add slide with layout
   111	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[TITLE_CONTENT]
   112	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   113	```
   114	
   115	### Adding Content
   116	
   117	#### Title Slide
   118	```python
   119	slide_layout = prs.slide_layouts[0]  # Title slide
   120	slide = prs.slides.add_slide(slide_layout)
   121	
   122	title = slide.shapes.title
   123	subtitle = slide.placeholders[1]
   124	
   125	title.text = "Quarterly Report"
   126	subtitle.text = "Q4 2024 Performance Review"
   127	```
   128	
   129	#### Text Content
   130	```python
   131	# Using placeholder
   132	body = slide.placeholders[1]
   133	tf = body.text_frame
   134	tf.text = "First bullet point"
   135	
   136	# Add more paragraphs
   137	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   138	p.text = "Second bullet point"
   139	p.level = 0
   140	
   141	p = tf.add_paragraph()
   142	p.text = "Sub-bullet"
   143	p.level = 1
   144	```
   145	
   146	#### Text Box
   147	```python
   148	from pptx.util import Inches, Pt
   149	
   150	left = Inches(1)
   151	top = Inches(2)
   152	width = Inches(4)
   153	height = Inches(1)
   154	
   155	txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
   156	tf = txBox.text_frame
   157	
   158	p = tf.paragraphs[0]
   159	p.text = "Custom text box"
   160	p.font.bold = True
   161	p.font.size = Pt(18)
   162	```
   163	
   164	#### Shapes
   165	```python
   166	from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
   167	
   168	# Rectangle
   169	shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
   170	    MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE,
   171	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # left, top
   172	    Inches(3), Inches(1.5) # width, height
   173	)
   174	shape.text = "Rectangle with text"
   175	
   176	# Common shapes:
   177	# MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   178	# MSO_SHAPE.OVAL, CHEVRON, ARROW_RIGHT
   179	# MSO_SHAPE.CALLOUT_ROUNDED_RECTANGLE
   180	```
   181	
   182	#### Images
   183	```python
   184	# Add image
   185	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   186	    'image.png',
   187	    Inches(1), Inches(2),  # position
   188	    width=Inches(4)        # auto height
   189	)
   190	
   191	# Or specify both dimensions
   192	slide.shapes.add_picture(
   193	    'logo.png',
   194	    Inches(8), Inches(0.5),
   195	    Inches(1.5), Inches(0.75)
   196	)
   197	```
   198	
   199	### Tables
   200	```python
   201	# Create table
   202	rows, cols = 4, 3
   203	left = Inches(1)
   204	top = Inches(2)
   205	width = Inches(8)
   206	height = Inches(2)
   207	
   208	table = slide.shapes.add_table(rows, cols, left, top, width, height).table
   209	
   210	# Set column widths
   211	table.columns[0].width = Inches(2)
   212	table.columns[1].width = Inches(3)
   213	table.columns[2].width = Inches(3)
   214	
   215	# Add headers
   216	headers = ['Product', 'Q3 Sales', 'Q4 Sales']
   217	for i, header in enumerate(headers):
   218	    cell = table.cell(0, i)
   219	    cell.text = header
   220	    cell.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.bold = True
   221	
   222	# Add data
   223	data = [
   224	    ['Widget A', '$10,000', '$12,500'],
   225	    ['Widget B', '$8,000', '$9,200'],
   226	    ['Widget C', '$15,000', '$18,000'],
   227	]
   228	for row_idx, row_data in enumerate(data, 1):
   229	    for col_idx, value in enumerate(row_data):
   230	        table.cell(row_idx, col_idx).text = value
   231	```
   232	
   233	### Charts
   234	```python
   235	from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   236	from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   237	
   238	# Chart data
   239	chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   240	chart_data.categories = ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4']
   241	chart_data.add_series('Sales', (19.2, 21.4, 16.7, 23.8))
   242	chart_data.add_series('Expenses', (12.1, 15.3, 14.2, 18.1))
   243	
   244	# Add chart
   245	x, y, cx, cy = Inches(1), Inches(2), Inches(8), Inches(4)
   246	chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   247	    XL_CHART_TYPE.COLUMN_CLUSTERED,
   248	    x, y, cx, cy, chart_data
   249	).chart
   250	
   251	# Customize
   252	chart.has_legend = True
   253	chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
   254	```

   256	### Formatting
   257	
   258	#### Text Formatting
   259	```python
   260	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   261	
   262	run = p.runs[0]
   263	run.font.name = 'Arial'
   264	run.font.size = Pt(24)
   265	run.font.bold = True
   266	run.font.italic = True
   267	run.font.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x66, 0xCC)
   268	```
   269	
   270	#### Shape Fill & Line
   271	```python
   272	from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
   273	
   274	shape.fill.solid()
   275	shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x80, 0x00)
   276	
   277	shape.line.color.rgb = RGBColor(0x00, 0x00, 0x00)
   278	shape.line.width = Pt(2)
   279	```
   280	
   281	#### Paragraph Alignment
   282	```python
   283	from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN
   284	
   285	p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER  # LEFT, RIGHT, JUSTIFY
   286	```
   287	
   288	## Best Practices
   289	
   290	1. **Use Templates**: Start with a .pptx template for consistent branding
   291	2. **Layout First**: Plan slide structure before coding
   292	3. **Reuse Slide Masters**: Maintain consistency across presentations
   293	4. **Optimize Images**: Compress images before adding
   294	5. **Test Output**: Always verify generated presentations
   295	
   296	## Common Patterns
   297	
   298	### Slide Deck Generator
   299	```python
   300	def create_deck(title, slides_content):
   301	    prs = Presentation()
   302	    
   303	    # Title slide
   304	    slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[0])
   305	    slide.shapes.title.text = title
   306	    
   307	    # Content slides
   308	    for slide_data in slides_content:
   309	        slide = prs.slides.add_slide(prs.slide_layouts[1])
   310	        slide.shapes.title.text = slide_data['title']
   311	        
   312	        body = slide.placeholders[1]
   313	        tf = body.text_frame
   314	        for i, point in enumerate(slide_data['points']):
   315	            if i == 0:
   316	                tf.text = point
   317	            else:
   318	                p = tf.add_paragraph()
   319	                p.text = point
   320	    
   321	    return prs
   322	```
   323	
   324	### Data-Driven Charts
   325	```python
   326	def add_bar_chart(slide, title, categories, values):
   327	    from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
   328	    from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE
   329	    
   330	    chart_data = CategoryChartData()
   331	    chart_data.categories = categories
   332	    chart_data.add_series('Values', values)
   333	    
   334	    chart = slide.shapes.add_chart(
   335	        XL_CHART_TYPE.BAR_CLUSTERED,
   336	        Inches(1), Inches(2),
   337	        Inches(8), Inches(4),
   338	        chart_data
   339	    ).chart
   340	    
   341	    chart.chart_title.text_frame.text = title
   342	    return chart
   343	```

   345	## Examples
   346

   399	### Example 2: Report with Data Table
   400	```python

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""
Build the 8-slide HTTP Archive State of the Web 2020-2025 presentation.
Follows task_input.json structure and source_brief.md data exactly.
"""

import os
from pptx import Presentation
from pptx.util import Inches, Pt, Emu
from pptx.enum.text import PP_ALIGN, MSO_ANCHOR
from pptx.enum.shapes import MSO_SHAPE
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
from pptx.enum.chart import XL_CHART_TYPE, XL_LEGEND_POSITION
from pptx.chart.data import CategoryChartData
from pptx.enum.dml import MSO_THEME_COLOR

# Ensure output dir exists
os.makedirs("/app/output", exist_ok=True)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Color palette — dark, analytical, data-forward
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
BG_DARK      = RGBColor(0x1A, 0x1F, 0x2E)  # deep navy/slate
BG_SLATE     = RGBColor(0x22, 0x2A, 0x3B)  # slightly lighter for cards
ACCENT_CYAN  = RGBColor(0x38, 0xB2, 0xAC)  # teal/cyan for desktop
ACCENT_AMBER = RGBColor(0xF6, 0xAD, 0x55)  # amber for mobile / highlights
ACCENT_GREEN = RGBColor(0x48, 0xBB, 0x78)  # green for positive trends
WHITE        = RGBColor(0xFF, 0xFF, 0xFF)
LIGHT_GRAY   = RGBColor(0xA0, 0xAE, 0xC0)
MED_GRAY     = RGBColor(0x68, 0x78, 0x8C)
DARK_GRAY    = RGBColor(0x4A, 0x55, 0x66)
RED_ACCENT   = RGBColor(0xE2, 0x53, 0x4F)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Helpers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

def set_slide_bg(slide, color):
    """Set solid background color for a slide."""
    background = slide.background
    fill = background.fill
    fill.solid()
    fill.fore_color.rgb = color

def add_textbox(slide, left, top, width, height, text, font_size=Pt(14),
                font_color=WHITE, bold=False, font_name="Segoe UI",
                align=PP_ALIGN.LEFT, valign=MSO_ANCHOR.TOP):
    """Add a text box with full formatting control."""
    txBox = slide.shapes.add_textbox(left, top, width, height)
    tf = txBox.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = text
    p.font.size = font_size
    p.font.color.rgb = font_color
    p.font.bold = bold
    p.font.name = font_name
    p.alignment = align
    tf.paragraphs[0].space_after = Pt(0)
    tf.paragraphs[0].space_before = Pt(0)
    return txBox

def add_card(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color=BG_SLATE,
             line_color=ACCENT_CYAN, line_width=Pt(1)):
    """Add a rounded rectangle card shape."""
    shape = slide.shapes.add_shape(
        MSO_SHAPE.ROUNDED_RECTANGLE, left, top, width, height
    )
    shape.fill.solid()
    shape.fill.fore_color.rgb = fill_color
    shape.line.color.rgb = line_color
    shape.line.width = line_width
    return shape

def add_stat_callout(slide, left, top, width, height, stat, label,
                     stat_color=WHITE, label_color=LIGHT_GRAY,
                     stat_size=Pt(54), label_size=Pt(14)):
    """Add a big stat number with a label underneath inside a card."""
    card = add_card(slide, left, top, width, height, fill_color=BG_SLATE,
                    line_color=DARK_GRAY, line_width=Pt(0.5))
    # Stat number
    tf = card.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = stat
    p.font.size = stat_size
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = stat_color
    p.font.name = "Segoe UI"
    p.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
    # Label
    p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
    p2.text = label
    p2.font.size = label_size
    p2.font.color.rgb = label_color
    p2.font.name = "Segoe UI"
    p2.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER
    p2.space_before = Pt(4)
    return card

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Presentation init — 16:9
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
prs = Presentation()
prs.slide_width = Inches(13.333)
prs.slide_height = Inches(7.5)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Slide 1: Title
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
blank_layout = prs.slide_layouts[6]  # blank
slide1 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)
set_slide_bg(slide1, BG_DARK)

# Accent bar at top
bar = slide1.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0), Inches(0),
                               Inches(13.333), Inches(0.15))
bar.fill.solid()
bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_CYAN
bar.line.fill.background()

# Title
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(2.2), Inches(11.333), Inches(1.2),
            "State of the Web 2020–2025",
            font_size=Pt(48), bold=True, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Subtitle
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(3.4), Inches(11.333), Inches(0.8),
            "HTTP Archive Trends in Page Weight, Protocols, and Security",
            font_size=Pt(24), font_color=ACCENT_CYAN, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Meta line
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(4.4), Inches(11.333), Inches(0.6),
            "Data Source: HTTP Archive — State of the Web Report  |  Jan 2020 – Mar 2026",
            font_size=Pt(14), font_color=LIGHT_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# Audience tag
add_textbox(slide1, Inches(1), Inches(5.2), Inches(11.333), Inches(0.5),
            "Audience: Web Performance Engineers & Front-End Architects",
            font_size=Pt(12), font_color=MED_GRAY, align=PP_ALIGN.CENTER)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
slide2 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)

            "Crawl Sample Size Tripled: From ~5M to 16M Desktop URLs Since 2020",
            font_size=Pt(28), bold=True)

add_textbox(slide2, Inches(0.5), Inches(0.95), Inches(12), Inches(0.4),
            "HTTP Archive continuously crawls millions of URLs. The sample jumped sharply in mid-2022 and has stabilized near 16M desktop / 12.5M mobile.",
            font_size=Pt(13), font_color=LIGHT_GRAY)

# Chart: dual-line time-series for sample size
chart_data = CategoryChartData()
chart_data.categories = ['Jan 2020', 'Mid 2021', 'Mid 2022', 'Mid 2023', 'Early 2026']
chart_data.add_series('Desktop', (5.0, 6.0, 15.0, 16.0, 16.0))
chart_data.add_series('Mobile',  (3.5, 4.5, 10.0, 12.5, 12.5))

chart = slide2.shapes.add_chart(
    XL_CHART_TYPE.LINE_MARKED,
    Inches(0.5), Inches(1.6), Inches(12.333), Inches(5.2),
    chart_data

chart.has_legend = True
chart.legend.position = XL_LEGEND_POSITION.BOTTOM
chart.legend.include_in_layout = False
chart.category_axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(11)
chart.category_axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY
chart.value_axis.tick_labels.font.size = Pt(11)
chart.value_axis.tick_labels.font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY
chart.value_axis.axis_title.text_frame.text = "Millions of URLs"
chart.value_axis.axis_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.size = Pt(11)
chart.value_axis.axis_title.text_frame.paragraphs[0].font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY

# Color series lines
from pptx.dml.color import RGBColor
chart.series[0].format.line.color.rgb = ACCENT_CYAN
chart.series[1].format.line.color.rgb = ACCENT_AMBER

slide3 = prs.slides.add_slide(blank_layout)

            font_size=Pt(13), font_color=LIGHT_GRAY)

items = [
    ("1. Page weight keeps climbing",
     "Median desktop pages now transfer ~2,000 KB — roughly 25% heavier than 2020. The 75th percentile exceeds 4,000 KB."),
    ("2. HTTPS is the new baseline",
     "At 99.2% desktop / 99.1% mobile, unencrypted HTTP is effectively extinct on the modern web."),
    ("3. HTTP/3 is the fastest-growing protocol metric",
     "From near-zero to ~39–40% support in under four years. HTTP/3 is rapidly becoming mainstream."),
    ("4. Fewer TCP connections despite more requests",
     "Multiplexing in HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 cut median connections per page by 14–27%, improving network efficiency."),
    ("5. Font-display still underused",
     "At ~40–42% adoption, most pages still risk FOIT. Significant room for improvement in font-loading UX.")
]

y_start = Inches(1.6)
for i, (title, body) in enumerate(items):
    row = i // 2
    col = i % 2
    x = Inches(0.5 + col * 6.2)
    y = y_start + row * Inches(2.3)
    card = add_card(slide8, x, y, Inches(5.9), Inches(2.0),
                    fill_color=BG_SLATE, line_color=DARK_GRAY, line_width=Pt(0.5))
    tf = card.text_frame
    tf.word_wrap = True
    p = tf.paragraphs[0]
    p.text = title
    p.font.size = Pt(15)
    p.font.bold = True
    p.font.color.rgb = ACCENT_CYAN
    p.font.name = "Segoe UI"
    p2 = tf.add_paragraph()
    p2.text = body
    p2.font.size = Pt(12)
    p2.font.color.rgb = LIGHT_GRAY
    p2.font.name = "Segoe UI"
    p2.space_before = Pt(6)

# CTA bar at bottom
cta_bar = slide8.shapes.add_shape(MSO_SHAPE.RECTANGLE, Inches(0.5), Inches(6.35),
                                   Inches(12.333), Inches(0.7))
cta_bar.fill.solid()
cta_bar.fill.fore_color.rgb = ACCENT_CYAN
cta_bar.line.fill.background()
tf_cta = cta_bar.text_frame
p_cta = tf_cta.paragraphs[0]
p_cta.text = "Call to Action: Benchmark your own sites against these baselines and prioritize the gaps."
p_cta.font.size = Pt(16)
p_cta.font.bold = True
p_cta.font.color.rgb = BG_DARK
p_cta.font.name = "Segoe UI"
p_cta.alignment = PP_ALIGN.CENTER

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Save
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
prs.save('/app/output/final_deck.pptx')
print("Saved /app/output/final_deck.pptx")
